lesson.subtitle: Lesson 2 -- Inside the Shop
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Camillo Furlan Alfredini | Lesson 2 -- Inside the Shop
lesson.grammar_point: there is / there are (affirmative, negative and questions)

listenings.text: Hello, and thank you for calling Weber Auto Service in Munich. We are open from seven a.m. to six p.m., Monday to Friday. There is a free waiting room with coffee and Wi-Fi. There are six lifts, so the service is fast. Is there a problem with your tires? There is a tire center next door. Thank you, and have a good day.

Hi, I am Klaus Weber, and this is my repair shop. It is not big, but it is busy. There are four mechanics and one manager. There is a big room for spare parts. On Monday there are not many customers, but on Friday there are a lot. My favorite tool is an old wrench. It is from my father.

extra_audio.text: After the fair, Laura takes Camillo to a repair shop in Munich. There is a small reception at the door. There is a waiting room with free coffee. There are six lifts and many tools. There is a big room for spare parts. Camillo takes photos for his shops in Brazil.

reading.rtitle: A Morning at Weber Auto Service
paras: After the fair in Frankfurt, Laura takes Camillo to Munich. There is a repair shop there, Weber Auto Service. It is a partner of her brand. The owner is Klaus Weber.

There is a small reception at the door, and there is a waiting room with free coffee and Wi-Fi. In the big room, there are six lifts. There are a lot of tools on the walls, and every tool has a place. There is one car with no engine: the engine is on the floor!

At the back, there is a room for spare parts, with boxes from many brands. There are no tires in the shop: the tires are in a tire center next door. Camillo takes a lot of photos. There are good ideas here for his three shops in Brazil.
